subject: Social Media
title: WhatsApp and Private Sharing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on WhatsApp and Private Sharing.

hook.text: WhatsApp replaced SMS in most of the world. Two billion users send 100 billion messages daily. Quietly.

buildup.text: Founded in 2009 by two ex-Yahoo engineers. No ads. No games. Just messaging. Simplicity was the strategy.

discovery.text: Facebook bought it for $19 billion in 2014. The founders wanted privacy. Facebook wanted data. A clash brewed.

twist.text: Both founders left over privacy disputes. Facebook integrated WhatsApp data anyway. Privacy lost.

climax.text: WhatsApp showed social media's future may be private—group chats, not public feeds. Dark social grew.

punchline.text: The biggest social network is the one you don't see.

quiz.question: How much did Facebook pay for WhatsApp?
